identity: Tennis player and fashion designer · United Kingdom · 1909–1995
title: Fred Perry's birth chart
metaDescription: Fred Perry's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.9° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 12.5° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Taurus, but precisely: 26.9°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 19.0° Gemini, Venus holds 2.1° Gemini, Mars holds 25.3° Aquarius — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.5° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Mars trine Pluto at 0.7°, and the Sun square Mars at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Uranus opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Taurus at 12.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Gemini at 19.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Virgo at 5.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aries at 18.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 4 air, 1 fire, 1 water by element and 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 3 cardinal by modality. Uranus was retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.5° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 12.5°.
